implemented.name: getCurrentAdminStatus
implemented.notes: Answers from the authoritative admins/{oid} registry record (not token claims — strictly harder to spoof than the source). Returns the source response shape incl. the permissions array the frontend gates UI on. A 200 is an ANSWER (isAdmin true or false because the registry was read); a 401 or 500 is a check that could not run, and the frontend must render those as 'unknown' rather than as a denial (#503) — requireUser denies only with 401, so a non-200 here is never an authorization verdict. The isAdmin:false answer also carries canBootstrap, the server's own verdict on whether bootstrapCurrentUserAdmin would succeed, so the UI offers that button only when it would work and never to an account that already has a registry row.

implemented.name: getAuthExpectations
implemented.notes: Since #515 every guarded route additionally requires the delegated scope `access_as_admin` in `scp`, and the verifier asserts `tid`, `iss`/`tid` agreement and `ver == 2.0`; the v1 `sts.windows.net` issuer is no longer accepted. A token with no `scp` (an ID token) is a 401 with a `missing-scope` audit row. Since #519 it also reports `requiredScope`, `requiredTokenVersion` and `labAgentAppRole`, each read from the guard's own constant rather than a copy, and the Integrations page renders them beside the credential inventory. Admin → Diagnostics (#355): the values the guard actually enforces — { expectedAudience: ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE, tenantId: ENTRA_TENANT_ID, adminAppRole: 'Admin', registryContainer: 'admins' } — so the page can compare the token it decodes in the browser against the API as deployed rather than against a frontend constant. requireUser, not requireRole, because the caller being diagnosed may hold the App Role and be missing from the registry. Discloses nothing a valid token does not already carry.

implemented.name: publerProxy
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/rest-proxy.js — authenticated pass-through to Publer at https://app.publer.com/api/v1, credentialed from PUBLER_API_KEY + PUBLER_WORKSPACE_ID. The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected.

implemented.name: linkieProxy

The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected. Additionally allowlisted to the endpoints the admin page calls — /profiles, /analytics/traffic-stats and the profile-scoped posts routes — because the API key's scopes are broader than any one screen needs. Base URL and allowlist taken from Site-Main functions/cms/proxies.js rather than inferred.

implemented.name: connectionProbe
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/connection-probe.js — the Integrations page's connection test for the services whose credentials are read only on the server: Telegram (GET /bot<token>/getMe), RSS.com (GET https://api.rss.com/v4/podcasts), YouTube (GET youtube/v3/search, maxResults=1), Resend (GET https://api.resend.com/domains, which a sending-access-only key is refused, so a pass proves the key can manage contacts and broadcasts) and Qlty (GET https://api.qlty.sh/user, #569). Entra editor-gated. UNLIKE the REST proxies, the caller supplies only a NAME — {probe:'telegram'|'rsscom'|'youtube'|'resend'|'qlty'} — and the URL, method and headers are built server-side from a frozen table, so there is no caller-supplied component in the outbound request at all rather than a validated one. Telegram and YouTube authenticate in the URL, so the upstream response is redacted before it is parsed and the built URL is never returned or logged. Only Telegram records a key verdict (getMe takes the token alone and answers 401 for a bad one); RSS.com's 401/403 split is unmeasured, YouTube answers 403 for an exceeded quota as well as a bad key, Resend refuses a sending-only key as well as a wrong one, and a Qlty 403 could be a token scope, so none of those four turns a light red. The YouTube probe costs ~100 of 10,000 daily quota units, which is why it is a button and never a timer. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED.

Response { ok, draft: { title, summary, postContent, summaryPrompt, detailsPrompt, keyTopics, suggestedContentType, sourceUrls } }.

implemented.name: createContentFromRecording
implemented.implementation: lib/content/draft-from-recording.js — one recording transcript into a content draft. Validates {recordingId, contentType ∈ blog_post|technical_guide|linkedin_post|podcast_notes|meeting_summary, title?, transcript?, provider?}; reads recordings/{id} (404 when absent), takes the transcript from the body or the stored recording (422 under 200 chars, 413 over 400k), infers 'Cloud Provider' from title+transcript with the URL drafter's keyword map, then one createDrafter().generateDraft call — the same drafter as generateArticleDraft/forge, feature-gated as forgeDrafting, with the content type's instruction block as customInstructionPrompt — and persists through createContentDocument, the createContentItem write path (dedup 409, quality gate, document shape; critique deferred to review). Patches the recording to status 'routed' with contentId/routedAt server-side so the link survives a client that dies before its own PATCH. Editor-gated; 75 s budget under the client's 90 s timeout; errors 400/404/413/422 input, 409/422 from persistence, 503 AI disabled or unconfigured, 504 budget, 502 generation. The request's provider hint is recorded as requestedAiProvider, never honoured as routing — the router's configured order decides and aiProvider records what ran. Response { ok, contentId, draft: { title, summary, keyTopics, aiProvider, cloudProvider } }.

endpoints.query: anonymous media delivery through the Function App's managed identity; immutable cache headers; conditional requests. Byte ranges (#349, ADR 0029): a single `Range: bytes=…` answers 206 with Content-Range from a ranged blob download (only the requested bytes are read), a start past the end answers 416 with `bytes */size`, multi-range requests are ignored and served in full, and every success carries `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. HEAD returns the 200's headers with Content-Length and no body, from blob properties alone.

endpoints.query: None. 'The Hybrid Lab right now' for /education/labs (#664, ADR 0032 decision 3). The Function App's own managed identity queries Azure Resource Graph under Reader on rg-lab-hybrid-prod-cus only (infra/lab-hybrid.tf): the one microsoft.hybridcompute/machines row (status, lastStatusChange, agentVersion, osName — never the machine name, which is the hostname) and a summarize of microsoft.policyinsights/policystates by complianceState for that group. Answers { configured: false } when the query returns no machine — group absent or empty — so the card reads 'not yet provisioned' rather than an invented row; otherwise { configured: true, arc { status, lastHeartbeatAt, agentVersion, osName }, policy { compliant, nonCompliant } | null, agent { online, queued } | null, coder { reachable, running, max } | null, asOf }. lastHeartbeatAt is Arc's lastStatusChange (ARM exposes no heartbeat time); null in a side block means that read failed, never zero. An Arc read failure answers 503 rather than 'not provisioned'. Success and 503 are both cached one minute in tool_service_cache, so anonymous traffic cannot drive the management plane (lib/labs/estate.js, lib/labs/resource-graph.js).

Order of bounds: the canonical body (results sorted by provider) is sha256-hashed and explain:<hash> read first — a hit answers { success: true, explanation: { text, model, generatedAt, cached: true } } with Cache-Control public max-age=3600 and no model call; then 503 'Explanations are not available' when the router cannot serve the pricingExplain feature (no key, every provider disabled, or the feature switched off on AI Engine → AI features — the owner's off switch for the one anonymous AI call), before any counter moves; then 403 unverified origin; then 5 per hashed client per hour through enforceSubmissionQuota (429 'Too many requests', Retry-After 3600); then 200 per UTC day across everyone through incrementIf on explain-quota:<day> (503 'Explanations are paused for today'). Then one generateTextResponse on the router's default chain, purpose general, with a fixed system prompt (two paragraphs, only the numbers given, cheapest and by how much, what the extras add, one thing that could flip it, <= 180 words) and the canonical JSON as the user message; the text has anything URL-shaped stripped, is stored with a 7-day ttl, and answers { success: true, explanation: { text, model, generatedAt, cached: false } }. 502 when the model returns nothing. endpoints.implementation: One registration, method fan-out. GET returns the issue, the email exactly as it would send (in the chosen Resend template when settings.templateId is set, merged by template-layout.js; otherwise, or when that template cannot be fetched or used, renderIssue with the stored settings, with templateProblem saying why and readyToSend false; the footer shows a visible placeholder until a postal address is saved), missingSettings, and the send plan resolveSendTime computes. GET returns issue.etag. GET's issue carries preheader (empty when unset); renderIssue emits it as the hidden inbox-preview block at the top of the email body, so approve sends it. PATCH accepts only {customNote (<=2000), subject (1-120), preheader (<=150, whitespace collapsed; empty clears it), sections, etag} on a draft; any other field is 400. sections may only remove items, reorder items within a section, reorder sections or remove whole sections: each submitted section is matched to a stored one by id and each item to a stored item in that section by url, any other field sent must equal the stored value, duplicates are refused, and the STORED items are written in the submitted order; an added, moved or edited item or section, or an issue left with no items, is 400 SECTIONS_INVALID; itemCount is recomputed. etag is REQUIRED (400 ETAG_REQUIRED without it), an etag that is not the stored one is 409 ISSUE_CHANGED before any write, the replace itself is ETag-conditional, and the response carries the new etag. DELETE (editor) takes body {etag} REQUIRED; only a draft or rejected issue, otherwise 409; it writes status deleted with deletedAt/deletedBy through an ETag-conditional replace, so it cannot race an approval that already claimed the issue, and answers {ok, id}. A deleted issue is a 404 on every route and is rebuilt from scratch by the builder. Issue ids are issue-YYYY-MM-DD; anything else is a 404 before Cosmos is read. When Newsletter settings name a Resend template (templateId, #557), every response that carries a preview renders it in that template (lib/newsletter/template-layout.js: the body at {{{NEWSLETTER_BODY}}}, escaped subject/preheader/period markers, the postal address and {{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}} appended when the template lacks them), fetched through GET /templates/{id} with a 5-minute in-process cache per id (template-source.js). A template that cannot be fetched or used, or RESEND_API_KEY unset, gives the built-in design plus templateProblem {code, message}; templateProblem is null otherwise.

PUBLISHER: it emails every confirmed subscriber. Body {etag} REQUIRED (400 ETAG_REQUIRED); then 503 NEWSLETTER_SENDING_DISABLED, before any read or Resend call, unless NEWSLETTER_SENDING_ENABLED is exactly "true" (Terraform newsletter_sending_enabled, default false; GET reports it as sendingEnabled); an etag that is not the stored one is 409 ISSUE_CHANGED, so an issue edited after the approver opened it is not sent. 409 SETTINGS_INCOMPLETE until the postal address and reply-to are saved; 503 without RESEND_API_KEY; 409 unless a draft. The send slot and the rendered email are worked out BEFORE the claim (409 SETTINGS_INVALID if the slot cannot be), so nothing on the site's side can strand an issue in sending. Claims the issue draft -> sending with an ETag-conditional replace before calling Resend, so simultaneous approvals create one broadcast. Creates the broadcast to the Newsletter segment from newsletter@news.hybridcloudworks.com with send:true and scheduled_at at the configured slot (DST-correct), or immediately when that slot is more than 72 h away. The outcome is written only while the issue is still the claim: success -> scheduled or sent with broadcastId; a Resend refusal -> draft with lastError and approval cleared, 502; no answer from Resend at all (timeout) -> stays sending with lastError, 502 SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, because a broadcast may exist; accepted but not recorded -> 200 with the usual issue payload (re-read, so it shows sending) plus warning; logs carry the invocation id and an error's name and code only, never issue or broadcast ids or SDK messages; a reject that landed mid-send stands and the answer is 409 CHANGED_DURING_SEND naming the broadcast. A process that dies mid-send leaves sending, never retried automatically. With a Resend template chosen in Newsletter settings (#557), the broadcast html is the issue merged into that template; if the template cannot be fetched or used, approval is refused with 409 TEMPLATE_UNUSABLE (and templateProblem) after the send-slot check and BEFORE the claim, so nothing is claimed or sent in a design other than the one chosen. The plain text is always the built-in rendering.

endpoints.implementation: functions/src/functions/platform-settings-http.js + lib/platform-settings.js getHistory; editor. Query ?setting=&limit=&after=, every refusal a 400 before Cosmos: setting must be a name in the spec registry (own key), limit a whole number 1..100 (default 50), after an ISO timestamp. Parameterised SQL: SELECT TOP @limit c.id, c.timestamp, c.userId, c.userName, c.details FROM c WHERE c.action = @action [AND c.details.setting = @setting] [AND c.timestamp < @after] ORDER BY c.timestamp DESC, cross-partition (the container partitions on /id; action and timestamp are indexed, details.setting is evaluated over the action's matches). Returns { entries: [{ id, at, actor, setting, summary }], nextAfter }: actor is the stored display name (userName, written on rows from #571 on) or else the Entra object id, and never userEmail or any email-shaped value; summary is the recorded details minus setting, scalars and lists of scalars only; nextAfter is the last entry's at when a full page came back, else null. The {setting} GET template answers the literal segment history the same way, since the host's precedence between the two routes is not relied on. The failure log names no query value.

endpoints.implementation: functions/src/functions/publish-http.js + lib/cms/set-slug.js; publisher; body { contentId, slug } — those two and nothing else; runs processPublishContent with reason 'set-slug' (lib/cms/publish.js SET_SLUG_REASON), which slugify()s the value, probes querySlugHolders (c.slug OR c.Slug) through the same never-throwing slugHolders wrapper an ordinary publish uses — the strictness is in evaluateSlugChange, which reads that wrapper's null as a refusal where resolveSlug reads it as 'not established' — and writes slug, Slug and curatedSubpagePath/slugPageUrl/publishedUrl/publicUrl derived through resolveCuratedSubpagePath and toPublicUrl, plus updatedAt, in ONE patch conditioned on the read's ETag; never contentStatus, Live, the gates, the cover or social triggers, the dates or the forge stats
endpoints.responses: 200 { contentId, requested, changed: true, moved, fields, previousSlug, slug, curatedSubpagePath, publicUrl } when it wrote — `moved` distinguishes the two outcomes a write can have (true: the slug the site routes on is a different one now; false: a REPAIR, e.g. Slug brought into line with slug or URL fields that were never written, on an article whose published URLs had drifted from the slug it already serves), and `fields` names what the patch touched; 200 { contentId, requested, changed: false, reason, slug, curatedSubpagePath, publicUrl } when it wrote nothing — the article was already on that slug with matching URLs, or a lost ETag race, which the publish pipeline has always reported as a skip rather than an error; 400 slug absent, not a string, or normalising to nothing; 404 no such document; 409 the slug is held by another document (body carries heldBy), or this one is not published, or its published path cannot be computed — no stored curatedSubpagePath and no inferable provider, which is refused rather than half-written (owner decision on #412: a set-slug that cannot compute the URL stops instead of writing a slug with no URL, deliberately diverging from the best-effort publish write); 503 the probe could not answer; 500 only for an unexpected failure. Every non-2xx means nothing was written.

signalrOption.fitAssessment: 20 connections is ample for a single-operator admin. The 20k/day cap is the constraint: a 1 msg/sec stream exhausts it in ~5.5h, so it only fits EVENT-DRIVEN pushes (Cosmos change feed -> Functions output binding -> push on actual data change), never chatty streams.

no SLA means the realtime layer can degrade with no recourse - polling fallback must remain in the client regardless
